name: Detection library log-source taxonomy and target mix
notes: Drives which log source family each generated rule targets, and the overall
mix of the library. Edit 'weight' values to reshape the library - they are
relative, not required to sum to 100.
'platforms' lists the ATT&CK platforms a family can serve. A rule is only
assigned to a family if the technique actually supports one of those platforms,
'tactics' lists the ATT&CK tactics a family can realistically observe. A rule is
only assigned to a family when the technique matches BOTH platform and tactic -
otherwise you get impossible pairings (e.g. registry persistence via firewall logs)
which the model correctly refuses. '*' means all tactics.
so a Linux-only technique never produces a firewall-only or Windows rule.
NOTE ON EDR PRODUCTS: Chronicle's UDM normalises CrowdStrike, Sysmon, Defender
and SentinelOne into the same event types, so there is no separate
'crowdstrike' family - windows_endpoint and linux_endpoint already cover those
clients. Vendor-specific rules would reduce portability.
WEIGHT RATIONALE (public sources, reviewed 2026-08):
- ASD/NSA joint 'Priority logs for SIEM ingestion' (2025) priority order:
EDR(1), network devices(2), Domain Controller(3), Active Directory(4),
Windows endpoint(5), virtualisation(6), cloud(8), containers(9),
Linux endpoint auditing(13), macOS(14).
- Practitioner consensus: authentication and cloud audit give the highest
detection value per GB; firewall and DNS are highest volume, lowest value/GB.
- Mandiant M-Trends 2026 (500k+ IR hours, 2025): exploits 32%, voice phishing
11%, prior compromise 10%, stolen credentials 9%, email phishing 6%. Cloud
intrusions: voice phishing 23%, third-party 17%, stolen creds 16%.
Also notes increased targeting of virtualisation and backup infrastructure.
- Cisco Talos IR Q1 2026: valid accounts = 24% of engagements.
=> Identity raised 10->16, Linux lowered 18->13, virtualisation 5->6,
firewall 20->17. Replace with real TELUS client distributions when available.
CAVEAT: the government guidance is enterprise-Windows-centric and ranks
ingestion order for one enterprise, not rule mix for an MSSP library. If TELUS
clients run large Linux fleets, raise linux_endpoint accordingly - actual client
telemetry should override these defaults.

families.label: Firewall / proxy / network perimeter
families.guidance: Firewall, proxy, and perimeter logs. Detect the network-observable behaviour: destination patterns, ports, protocol anomalies, connection volume and timing. Exclude internal address space with a reference list rather than hardcoded ranges. No endpoint process fields - a firewall log does not know the initiating process.

families.label: Windows endpoint (EDR / Sysmon / Security log)
families.guidance: Windows endpoint telemetry from any EDR (CrowdStrike, Defender, SentinelOne) or Sysmon - UDM normalises them, so never reference a vendor name. Windows conventions: process lineage, command lines, registry keys, service and scheduled-task creation.

families.label: Linux endpoint (EDR / auditd)
families.guidance: Linux endpoint telemetry from EDR or auditd. Use Linux conventions only: /etc, /var, /tmp, /proc, /dev/shm, cron paths, systemd units, shell history. Never Windows paths, .exe names, or registry keys.

families.label: IDS / IPS / network security appliance
families.guidance: IDS/IPS and network security appliance logs. Focus on detection/prevention verdicts, repeated blocked attempts, and traffic-pattern anomalies. Reference security_result fields cautiously - vendor mapping to UDM is inconsistent, so do not build core logic on security_result.action alone.

families.label: Identity provider (Entra ID / Okta / AD)
families.guidance: Identity provider sign-in and directory audit logs. Authentication anomalies, MFA patterns, privilege and group changes, service-principal or app-consent abuse. No endpoint process fields.

families.label: Cloud control plane (CloudTrail / Azure Activity / GCP Audit)
families.guidance: Cloud provider audit logs. API-level activity: resource creation and deletion, permission and policy changes, key and secret access, logging or guardrail tampering. No endpoint process fields.

families.label: Microsoft 365 / Google Workspace
families.guidance: Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace unified audit logs. Mailbox rule creation and forwarding, mass file access or download, sharing-permission changes, tenant setting modification. No endpoint process fields.

families.label: VMware / ESXi / hypervisor
families.guidance: ESXi and hypervisor management logs (hostd, vmkernel, shell). SSH or shell enablement, datastore access, VM manipulation, host configuration changes, management-plane authentication.

families.label: Container runtime / Kubernetes
families.guidance: Container runtime and Kubernetes audit logs. Privileged or host-mounted container creation, exec into running containers, service-account token abuse, control-plane API calls.

families.label: DNS query / resolver logs
families.guidance: DNS query and resolver logs. Detect C2 and exfiltration patterns: high-entropy or algorithmically generated domains, abnormal query volume or record types (TXT/NULL), long subdomain labels, newly-observed domains. Exclude known-good domains via a reference list. No endpoint process fields.

families.label: macOS endpoint (EDR / unified log)
families.guidance: macOS endpoint telemetry from EDR or the unified log. Use macOS conventions only: launchd plists in /Library/LaunchAgents and /Library/LaunchDaemons, /Users/*/Library paths, osascript, xattr, codesign. Never Windows paths, .exe names, or registry keys. Ranked lowest priority in the ASD/NSA guidance - kept at minimal weight so macOS-only techniques still have a valid home rather than being mis-assigned to an impossible log source.
